Title: Thursday September 14, 2023 - Boulder City Council Study Session

Topic1.Title: Library District Intergovernmental Agreement Update and Direction
Topic1.Summary: Staff from the City Attorney's Office and City Manager's Office updated Council on separating the Municipal Library from the City and transferring assets and responsibilities to the new Boulder Public Library District. Council gave direction on two policy issues: a three-year, hybrid trustee appointment process, and a long-term lease of city-owned library buildings with a district option to terminate at five-year intervals. Council also agreed that staff should bring the two-party IGA back within about 30 days.

Topic2.Title: 2024 Recommended Budget Overview and Funding Priorities
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the $514.8 million 2024 recommended budget, with general fund spending of $196.1 million, a 4.1% increase over 2023. Revenue concerns included slowing sales tax projections, a possible property tax ballot measure, and the expiring 0.15% general fund sales tax. Key investments covered behavioral health response, affordable housing, wildfire resilience, and city employee wages, and the six-year CIP totals about $900 million. Staff also noted large unfunded needs and proposed a long-term financial strategy.

Topic3.Title: Community Engagement and Feedback from Community Connectors
Topic3.Summary: Community Connectors Jamal Gilmore and Lenora Cooper presented findings from spring 2023 listening sessions that reached 74 participants, most of whom were people of color. Top community priorities included diverse housing types with a full range of affordability, financial security and economic opportunity, racial equity implementation, and mental health support. Staff said these priorities were shared with department directors before budget development and were reflected in the 2024 proposal. The Connectors asked for continued partnership, professional support, and more youth and mental health investment.

Topic4.Title: Council Questions, Budget Process, and Next Steps
Topic4.Summary: Council asked questions about revenue trends, pilot program accountability, snow and ice and pothole maintenance, the South Boulder Rec Center, staff compensation and living wage, and how outcome-based budgeting measures program effectiveness. Council members discussed using unspent funds, such as the day services center money, for immediate needs and emphasized the zero-sum nature of budget changes. Staff said Council feedback on proposed changes is due by September 25, with a first reading on October 5 and adoption two weeks later. The meeting closed at about 9:50 p.m.
